install.title: Install Nice Return Visits
install.wizard.detected: It looks like you're using {browser}. Select it below to confirm, or choose another browser.
install.wizard.unknown: We couldn't identify your browser. Select it below, or choose Another browser / I don't know.
install.wizard.switchBrowser: These instructions are for {browser}. If you are not already using it, open {browser}, visit nicereturnvisits.org, choose Open NRV, and start this guide again there. If you are already using it, select Next.
install.wizard.normalSafari: Use a normal Safari tab, not a Private tab. If this is a Private tab, close it and reopen NRV in a normal Safari tab before continuing.
install.wizard.safariShare: Tap Share: the square with an arrow pointing up.
install.wizard.safariShareTip: If Share is hidden, tap the three dots near the address bar, then tap Share. On iPad, look at the top of the screen.
install.wizard.safariHome: Scroll down and tap Add to Home Screen.
install.wizard.safariHomeTip: Scroll to the bottom of the Share menu. Tap Edit Actions to add Add to Home Screen if necessary; on iPad, tap View More if shown.
install.wizard.safariAdd: Turn on Open as Web App if offered, then tap Add.
install.wizard.edgeAndroidMenu: Tap the three-line menu at the bottom of Microsoft Edge.
install.wizard.samsungMenu: Tap the three-line menu at the bottom of Samsung Internet.
install.wizard.androidMenu: Tap the three dots in the browser, near the address bar.
install.wizard.chromeAndroidAction: Tap Install app. If you see Add to Home screen instead, tap that.
install.wizard.edgeAndroidAction: Tap Add to phone. If asked, choose Install app rather than Create shortcut.
install.wizard.firefoxAndroidAction: Tap Install in the Firefox menu.
install.wizard.samsungAction: Tap Add page to, then tap Home screen.
install.wizard.androidMenuTip: Look at the top or bottom edge of the browser. Tap once on the page if the browser controls are hidden.
install.wizard.androidActionTip: Scroll through the menu or swipe its rows to find the option. If it is unavailable, try Chrome in a normal tab and open NRV from nicereturnvisits.org.
install.wizard.androidConfirm: If a confirmation appears, tap Install or Add to finish.
install.wizard.edgeMenu: Click the three dots at the top right of Microsoft Edge.
install.wizard.chromeMenu: Click the three dots at the top right of Google Chrome.
install.wizard.desktopMenuTip: Look at the far right of the browser window, above this page.
install.wizard.edgeApps: Click Apps, then click Install this site as an app.
install.wizard.chromeApps: Click Cast, save, and share, then click Install page as app.
install.wizard.desktopInstallTip: If the option is missing, check for an install icon at the right end of the address bar. If neither appears, try a normal browser window and reload NRV.
install.wizard.desktopConfirm: In the confirmation window, click Install.
install.wizard.macSafari: At the top of your Mac screen, click File, then click Add to Dock.
install.wizard.macSafariTip: If Add to Dock is missing, update macOS and Safari, or open NRV in Google Chrome instead.
install.wizard.macSafariAdd: In the window that appears, click Add.
install.wizard.unsupportedApple: For a reliable installed icon, open Safari in a normal tab, visit nicereturnvisits.org, choose Open NRV, and start this guide again.
install.wizard.unsupported: This browser and device combination is not covered by this guide. Open Google Chrome in a normal window, visit nicereturnvisits.org, choose Open NRV, and start this guide again.
install.wizard.close: After installing, close this browser page. Then open NRV from its new icon and follow the setup or recovery prompts. If an NRV app window opened automatically, continue there instead. Select Next now for help finding the icon.
install.wizard.openComputer: Open Nice Return Visits from its new icon: look in the Start menu on Windows, the Dock or Applications on a Mac, or your computer's app launcher.
install.wizard.openMobile: Find the new NRV icon on your Home Screen and tap it.
install.wizard.openComputerTip: Search your computer for NRV or Nice Return Visits. If you cannot find it, go Back and check that installation finished.
install.wizard.openMobileTip: Swipe through your Home Screens or search for NRV. If it is not there, go Back and check that installation finished.
install.wizard.setup: In the installed NRV window, follow the prompts to continue setup or restore your previous information. If your contacts are in another copy, back up that copy and restore it here; check your contacts before removing the original.
install.browserDoorway: NRV is designed to be used from its Home Screen icon. This browser page is only the doorway to installation; it cannot be used to work with NRV contacts.
install.guidance: We’ll guide you through adding the NRV icon. After you open that icon, NRV will check for previous NRV information and continue setup or offer recovery choices.
install.general: Installation steps vary by device and browser. Look for an option such as “Install app” or “Add to Home Screen” in your browser menu. If you don’t see one, check your browser’s help for installing a website as an app.
install.browserUncertain: Safari could not be identified reliably. Use these steps only if you are using Safari.
install.iphoneShare: Tap Share (the square with an upward arrow). If Share is not visible, tap More (three dots) near the address bar, then Share.
install.iphoneAddHome: Scroll down and tap Add to Home Screen. If needed, use Edit Actions to add it to the Share menu.
install.ipadAddHome: Tap View More, then Add to Home Screen. You may need to scroll to find it.
install.openAsApp: Turn on Open as Web App if offered, then tap Add.
install.afterAdding: After adding the icon, return to this page if necessary and select the button below. Then close this page and open NRV from its icon.
install.safariWarning: Use normal Safari, not Private Browsing.
install.safariDetails: NRV cannot reliably identify Safari Private mode. If this page is in a Private tab, stop here, close that tab, and reopen NRV in a normal Safari tab. Private use is unsupported, and NRV cannot recover information created or lost in a Private session.
install.safariConfirm: I am using a normal Safari tab, not a Private tab.
install.scrollInstructions: Scroll down for instructions to install NRV to your Home Screen.
install.stepDots: Tap the three horizontal dots in the bottom-right corner.
install.stepShare: Tap Safari’s Share button (the square with an arrow pointing up).
install.stepMinimize: After adding, this screen may minimize.
install.stepReturn: Swipe up to bring this screen back.
install.stepOpen: Close this window, then tap the new NRV icon on your Home Screen.
install.returnToIcon: After Add to Home Screen, return to the icon—not to Contacts in Safari. Setup or restoration continues when NRV opens from the icon.
install.added: I added NRV to my Home Screen
install.complete: This part of installation is complete. Close this Safari tab or window. Find the NRV icon on your Home Screen and tap it to continue installation and setup.

install.openIcon: Install NRV to your device’s Home Screen, then close this browser page and open NRV from the new icon. Do not use this browser page as a second working copy.

backup.title: Backup
dropbox.explanation: Cloud backup keeps a copy of your contacts outside this device, in your own Dropbox, so you can recover them if your device is lost, broken or replaced. It is off unless you turn it on. Dropbox is entirely optional: the app works fully without it, and all your data can stay only on this device.
dropbox.recoveryCopy: Dropbox is the active backup and synchronization location. To preserve a protected recovery copy, use Dropbox’s own tools to copy or move a backup outside NRV’s Return Visits app folder. NRV cannot see or change that separate copy; download it later to restore it as a Local backup.
dropbox.signupExplanation: The app can send you to Dropbox to sign up, but it cannot create the account for you. The free Basic plan is enough.
dropbox.haveAccount: Do you already have a Dropbox account?
security.onDescription: A passphrase is on for this app copy. You may change it or turn it off.
security.offDescription: A passphrase is optional. It locks the app so only you can open it; it does not back anything up. A passphrase is currently off. Turn it on to encrypt the data on this device; you will be asked for it each time you open the app. Use at least {count} characters. You will be given a recovery code to keep; without the passphrase or that code, the data cannot be opened.
security.turnOffIntro: If you turn the passphrase off:
security.decryptPrefix: The contacts and settings on this device are decrypted and stored
security.decryptSuffix: Anyone who can open this browser or app on this device could read them.
security.opensDirectly: The app opens right away and no longer asks for a passphrase.
security.recoveryDisabled: Your recovery code stops working, because there is no passphrase left to recover.
security.futureBackups: Backups you make from now on, including Dropbox backups, are not encrypted. Backups you already made keep the passphrase they were created with.
security.canReenable: You can turn a passphrase on again at any time.
security.confirmCurrent: Enter your current passphrase (or recovery code) to confirm
recovery.explanation: A recovery code is a long random code you keep somewhere safe, away from this device. If you forget your passphrase, type the code in place of the passphrase to open the app. Anyone with the code can open your data, so treat it like the passphrase.
recovery.isSet: A recovery code is set for this app copy. It is stored, locked, inside your backups too. If you lost the code, make a new one below.
recovery.notSet: No recovery code is set yet. Make one now so a forgotten passphrase does not lock you out.
backup.protects: Backups protect you from losing your contacts.
backup.strategy: One device: Local backup is normally sufficient. Multiple devices: use Dropbox when you want NRV to coordinate them automatically. Keep a separate recovery copy somewhere NRV cannot manage.
backup.encryptionNote: Encrypted if a passphrase is on. You can also export from the Contacts page footer.
backup.localSurvives: A downloaded Local backup survives Erase All Data. For a protected recovery copy, keep a separate copy outside NRV’s working storage.

agreement.title: Before you use Nice Return Visits
agreement.intro: Please read and agree to both notices before using the app on this browser or installed-app copy.
agreement.notice.heading: Where your information goes
agreement.notice.body: Contacts are saved in this browser or installed-app copy. Dropbox stores a copy only if you choose to connect it. Some map and address-search features send the search information to outside providers. Sharing or exporting a contact sends a copy wherever you choose.
agreement.notice.small: Agreeing to these notices does not connect Dropbox or send a contact or address search.
agreement.checkbox: I have read and agree to the Terms of Use and Privacy & Data Notice.
unlock.firstUse.heading: First-time use
unlock.firstUse.body: Use the NRV Home Screen icon as your working copy. Before adding contacts, you can fill in Defaults & Your Details and add any Cities, Regions, and Areas you need.
unlock.firstUse.free: Nice Return Visits is free to use, with no app fees or subscription. Your internet or mobile provider may charge for data.
unlock.restore.prompt: Moving to a new device? Restore an encrypted backup instead.
unlock.noRecovery: Your data is encrypted with this passphrase. If you forget it, there is no recovery option.
settings.mapDefault: When the Map has no visible contact pins, it centers near this city. Its name and state are looked up with OpenStreetMap Nominatim while the Map is open.
settings.name: Name:
settings.yourDetailsNote: If you enter your name, it is added as “Shared by [your name]” to a message when you choose Share on a contact. The app prepares the message; you choose whether and to whom to send it. Your address and home pin are not included in that message. Your home appears on the Map as a house icon, and the Map opens fitted to include it. Looking up your address sends it to OpenStreetMap Nominatim only when you choose the lookup button. Your details stay on this device and are included in backups.
time.trackNote: Adds a Time button to the bottom bar with a Start/Stop timer and manual entry. Turning this off erases all recorded time.

location.howText: A city is divided into regions, which are large parts of the city (such as North, South, East, and West). A region is divided into areas, which are smaller neighborhoods within that region. Cities, regions, and areas are added as you enter them for yourself or a contact; use each field's + Add New choice to add one.
location.regionInstructions: You can also add a region while adding a contact. Choose + Add New Region... in that contact's Region list to add one for the selected City. A region name can be used in more than one city; the city you choose makes it unique.
location.manageNote: Cities, regions and areas are each listed once. Edit renames a region or area everywhere and lets you choose which cities it is assigned to. Delete is blocked while any contact uses it; deleting a city also removes its region and area assignments, after you confirm. Regions and areas are independent: a contact can have a city, a region, an area, or any combination.
location.contactCityNote: Select a saved city or choose + Add City to add one here.
location.regionHint: A region is a large part of a city, such as North or Downtown. Areas (neighborhoods) go inside a region.
location.areaHint: An area is a neighborhood or small section within the selected region.
location.provinceHint: Use this for the province associated with this locality, if known.
location.districtHint: Use this for the district within the selected province, if known.
map.addressHint: Entering or saving an address does not create a pin. Use the address or device location above. A city-only result is approximate. Move the pin on the map below or on the main Map; its coordinates will update.
map.coordinatesHint: Map coordinates are optional. Tap the map, drag the pin, or enter coordinates to adjust it. Device location does not change the address.
map.choosePin: Choose how to set the pin:
map.lookupPrivacy: Address and cross-street lookups send the entered location text to OpenStreetMap Nominatim when you choose a lookup button. When the Map is open, it looks up the City, State / Province, and Country of contacts without saved coordinates to show approximate city pins. Device location is requested when the Map opens and may be approximate. You can always adjust a contact's saved pin.

dropbox.folderBefore: . The app can only use its own folder, called
dropbox.folderAfter: , and cannot see anything else in your Dropbox.
dropbox.backupSchedule: The app backs up when you open it if your last backup is more than a day old, and shortly after you make changes. Dropbox keeps your latest copy plus up to 10 dated copies.
dropbox.multiDevice: Using more than one device? Each device combines its changes with Dropbox automatically: when you open the app, every couple of minutes while it is open, and as soon as the connection returns after being offline. Visits and contacts added on different devices are all kept. If you have no signal, your changes stay saved on the device and upload as soon as it can reach Dropbox. The cloud icon at the top shows the state (tap it to sync now). You can also tap Check for a Newer Backup.
dropbox.concurrentChanges: If two devices change the very same contact at the same time, the most recent change to that contact is used, but visits from both devices are kept.
settings.eraseWarning: Before erasing, create or verify a current backup and preserve a separate recovery copy outside NRV’s normal storage or Dropbox app folder. Erasing removes this copy’s contacts, settings, passphrase/security data, setup choices, and local Dropbox connection. Downloaded backup files and Dropbox files are not deleted. Removing the Home Screen icon alone does not necessarily erase NRV data.
